# Skill config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/inline-skills/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.SkillBlock` declaring one **skill**: a reusable instruction fragment, plus an additive tool list, registered under its label in the daemon's skill registry — the one the shared capability resolver answers `@skills:*` and explicit skill references from. The block label is the skill name and is what every reference resolves; one skill per file, and the file stem must equal the label (ADR-087 D3's recipe regime) — so `.tera/inline-skills/git-workflow.hcl` declares `skill "git-workflow"` and deleting that file is how the skill is retired.

**This is not `.tera/skills/`, and the difference is not cosmetic.** That directory holds *skill bundles* (PRD-012 §4.4): a directory per skill containing `SKILL.md`, with `references/`, `scripts/` and `tools/` beside it, loaded per session through the vault Mounter — a user vault's scripts and bundled tools register only when it holds the `exec` ability, an explicit grant bound in the system vault (ADR-147 D3, D7), while the system vault's own arriving executable surface keeps its per-apply `--allow-exec` acknowledgement — and referenced by the namespaced name `<vault-id>/skills/<dir>`. This kind is the *inline* one — the whole skill is the one HCL block, it never carries files, it composes onto the runtime `Root` like any other config kind, and it is referenced by the bare label. A name containing `/skills/` is a bundle and a bare name is one of these. No recipe kind names an inline skill in a `skills = [...]` list: the `agent` recipe kind and a worker's embedded `agent {}` block are refused at load by name (ADR-136). See the `skill` recipe reference for the bundle kind.

**This is the only place a `skill` block may be authored.** The bootstrap-HCL kernel spelling is retired (ADR-122 D5): a config file that still declares one is refused by name, with the diagnostic naming this directory. The move is what makes the surface reload at all — the diff and apply have existed since kottera/kottera#7, and with the kernel as the only authoring surface and no kernel file watcher, nothing could ever trigger them.

**A reload changes what runs NEXT.** `HandleSkillsReplaced` swaps the skill registry the capability resolver reads, under a write lock: a registry lookup already made keeps the set it saw, and the next one reads the new set (ADR-105 D1, ADR-122 D6, ADR-136 D3). Editing one skill leaves every other skill's definition untouched.

**Ownership is one-way, and the daemon latches it.** Once this directory exists in the vault, the vault owns the kind — so removing the last file here removes the skill rather than restoring some earlier set. The latch matters because git cannot track an empty directory: a checkout, a fresh clone or a `git rm` that removed the last file would otherwise flip ownership back on a reload, which is the resurrection D5 exists to prevent.

| Identity regime | `recipe` — the filename stem is the identity; the file declares exactly one resource, and a block label — where the grammar admits one — must equal the stem (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `skill` |
| Loader directory | `.tera/inline-skills/<name>.hcl` |

## Example

A minimal `inline-skills`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/inline-skills/example-skill.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

skill "example-skill" {
  instruction = "What this skill asks of a session, and how it should go about it."
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | block label | The skill's name, and the only name anything resolves it by — an explicit skill reference or an @skills:* expansion in the capability resolver. Under ADR-087 D3's recipe regime the file stem is the identity, so this label must equal it: .tera/inline-skills/git-workflow.hcl declares skill "git-workflow". A bare name like this one is an INLINE skill; a name containing /skills/ is a .tera/skills/ bundle, which is a different kind entirely. |
| `description` | string | no | — | — | — | A one-line summary, used for discovery and progressive disclosure. |
| `instruction` | string | yes | — | — | — | The instruction fragment this skill contributes — the prose the skill exists to carry. Editing it takes effect on the NEXT registry lookup: the skill registry is swapped under a write lock, so a lookup already made keeps the edition it saw (ADR-105 D1, ADR-122 D6). |
| `tools` | string[] | no | — | — | — | Additional tool or capability references this skill contributes, ADDITIVE to the tools of whatever names the skill rather than replacing them. Each name is resolved by the capability resolver like any other tool reference, so a name nothing provides contributes nothing rather than failing. |
